2. Heard learned counsel for the appellant.
3.

The present appeal has been filed by the appellant-insurance company against the judgment/award dated 12.05.2000 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (A.D.J. VIIIth),
Bareilly in M.A.C. No.372/1998.

sentences.text: It is contended that earlier the claim petition was allowed against the owner of the vehicle holding that the offending vehicle tractor No.UPL-8591 was not insured on the date of accident.

Subsequently after the award was passed, the owner of the vehicle filed restoration application to recall the order dated 21.04.1999 which was allowed by the Tribunal and the claim petition was restored.
Thereafter, the Tribunal again heard the claim petition and passed an award fastening the liability upon the insurance company to pay the compensation.
5. It is submitted that the Tribunal has acted illegally and without jurisdiction in recalling the earlier award dated 22.11.1999 inasmuch as the Tribunal has no power to review.

It is further submitted that the finding of the Tribunal that the vehicle was insured on the date of accident is perverse inasmuch as the insurance policy in respect of offending vehicle was issued on 22.06.1998 whereas the accident had taken place on 20.06.1998.
Accordingly, it is contended that the Tribunal has erred in law in fastening the liability upon the appellant to pay compensation.
6. Be that as it may, the record reveals that the appellant has not assailed the order of the Tribunal dated 22.11.1999 by which the Tribunal has recalled the award dated 21.04.1999.

In such view of the fact, the plea in respect of jurisdiction of Tribunal to recall the award dated 21.04.1999 cannot be raised in the present appeal, and therefore, the said plea being devoid of merit, is rejected.

7. So far as the issue with regard to insurance policy is concerned, the Tribunal has recorded finding that the agent of the Insurance Company had taken premium on 19.06.1998 and had issued cover note.
Accordingly, the Tribunal found that as the premium had been paid to the agent of the Insurance Company by the owner before the date of accident, the insurance Company could not deny its liability.
The Insurance Company has not disputed the fact that the person who acted as agent was his agent.
It has also been proved on record that the agent had taken premium on 19.06.1998 and issued cover note.
8. In such view of the fact, this Court does not find any illegality in the finding of the Tribunal holding that the vehicle was insured on the date of accident.
9. For the reasons given above, the appeal lacks merit and is accordingly dismissed.

Order Date :- 20.7.2023 R.S. Tiwari  United Insurance Company Ltd. vs Kishan Lal And Another on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130332218/
